instruction: The work is carried out with FEniCS from the command line. Design a high-conductivity heat path. For this task, run legacy FEniCS with `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/conda run --no-capture-output --prefix /home/user/miniconda3/envs/fenics-legacy python` when working on `heat_path_opt_base.py`. Read /home/user/Desktop/problem_spec.json for the domain, design grid, solver mesh, material conductivities, thermal boundary conditions, heat source, and material budget. Read /home/user/Desktop/baseline_conductivity_mask.csv as the initial feasible material mask. You may use /home/user/Desktop/heat_path_opt_base.py as the starter workflow. Create /home/user/Desktop/conductivity_mask.csv, /home/user/Desktop/solve_submission.py, and /home/user/Desktop/temperature.xdmf; if the XDMF writer creates a companion .h5 file, keep it in the same directory. The mask CSV must be 20 by 20, all values must be in [0, 1], and the high-conductivity material budget must not exceed 0.30 of the design cells. Keep the domain, material constants, heat source, boundary conditions, and material budget from the problem specification unchanged.
